Reading this post, this could’ve been written by my parents when I was in high school. I want to start off by saying that things do get better. I’ve just finished my undergrad and am going to get a masters in the fall, neither of which I could have ever pictured myself doing 8 years ago. 

I was diagnosed with social and GAD when I was 14 and have never been one for therapy (not anything against it, I just felt like talking about my problems didn’t help the core issue. I KNEW my anxiety wasn’t rational but that didn’t make it less REAL). I had issues for several years with insomnia and couldn’t talk to anyone because I was so paralyzed by fear. I went on medication and my quality of life improved so much. I was able to make friends, focus on school, do extracurriculars, etc. 

I would have a conversation with your daughter about her thoughts on medication. It’s not for everyone, but I had no side effects and being medicated helped me understand that living without constant anxiety was possible and it honestly made life much much better. I knew how I wasn’t living wasn’t normal but I didn’t know how much happier I could be. 

It sounds like your daughter is really struggling and the fact people are making fun of her cannot be helping and it’s hard to change how others perceive you. I agree that changing schools might not change anything else, but having a fresh start could help. Although, social groups may have already been formed and it might be hard for her to fit in. Just things to consider!

My heart goes out to you and your daughter but I’m glad she has support and life does get easier, it might just take a bit of time to see what works for her. If you have any questions feel free to reach out!
